**Starts** once #197 is merged.

## Why

Every worker is started and ends the same way, so this builds that once, before the first worker (#60). The coordinator starts a worker with the SDK's `Agent` tool. The worker ends by calling `report_result` with its problems and its questions for the user. Hooks record the worker's calls, and replace its last message with a result that code builds, so no free text from a worker reaches the coordinator (technical spec 6.5). It waits for #197, since until the coordinator runs as a named agent, it would be sent the worker tools this adds.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 6.5 (the settings, `report_result`, the three hooks, and the result's lines).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 1 (the `worker` server), 2.3 (`search_near` and `search_along_leg`), 2.6 (`report_result`), 3, and 4.
- [Research doc](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.8, for what was checked against Agent SDK 0.3.301, and the spike code on the [`spike/worker-182`](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/tree/spike/worker-182/worker-spike) branch.

## Open questions

- ~~**What should the query's `allowedTools` list, now that the definitions set what each agent is sent?** `allowedTools` lets a tool run without asking, and with `permissionMode: "dontAsk"` any other tool call is refused. It applies to the whole session, workers too. Today (after #197) it allows `mcp__trip`, `mcp__memory`, `mcp__routing`, and only `find_place` and `read_place` on the `places` server. So a worker's call to `search_near`, `search_along_leg`, or `report_result` would be refused, and `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch` aren't allowed either. One choice is to allow each whole server, plus the three built-in tools, since the definitions now keep each agent to its own tools (technical spec 6.5). The other is to name every tool one by one.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** allow each whole server, plus `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch` by name. The list covers the whole session, so it can't let a worker call a tool and refuse the coordinator the same tool. Only the definitions can do that. And every tool in the session belongs to some agent, since the query's `tools` and `strictMcpConfig` keep out everything else. So a tool-by-tool list would always end up as every tool in the session, kept by hand as a second copy of the definitions. When that copy falls behind, a worker's call is refused, and the trace looks like an agent problem when it's an app bug. `allowedTools` now only lets our tools run without a prompt, and the definitions decide who gets which tool. Write it into technical spec 6.5.

## Do

- Add `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch` to the query's `tools`. Only worker definitions list the web tools, so the coordinator isn't sent them (tool design section 1).
- Add the two settings to the Claude Code process's environment: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` and `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` (technical spec 6.5).
- Add the `worker` server with `report_result` (tool design 2.6), built for each turn like the other servers, and add it to the query's `mcpServers`.
- Put `search_near` and `search_along_leg` on the `places` server. The coordinator's definition doesn't list them, so it isn't sent them.
- Set the query's `allowedTools` to each of our servers, plus `Agent`, `WebSearch`, and `WebFetch`, and write the reason into technical spec 6.5 (see the settled question above).
- Add the three hooks from technical spec 6.5: the `PostToolUse` hook that records each worker's calls by `agent_id`, the `SubagentStop` hook that sends a worker back at most twice when it hasn't called `report_result`, and the `PostToolUse` hook on `Agent` that replaces the worker's last message with the result code builds. Each acts only for our worker types (technical spec section 1).
- Draft the result's wording (technical spec 6.5), for Joe to review in the PR.

## Done when

- Tests with fake SDK messages show the `Agent` hook builds each kind of result: candidate replies in call order, a "No candidates added for:" line, a "No weather saved for:" line, problems and questions or "none", the last `report_result` call counting when there are two, and the line for a worker that stopped without reporting.
- Tests show the `SubagentStop` hook sends a worker back at most twice, and ignores agent types that aren't our workers.
- The coordinator's view file still shows no worker tool, such as `search_near` or `report_result`.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
